newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX gasoline settles sharply higher in light day.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX gasoline settles sharply higher in light day.

text.p: NYMEX oil prices settled higher in light trade on Friday with gasoline assuming the title of king of the bulls, but traders said they still see more downside movement before the uptrend gets back under way.

"I still see some more downside potential before we head back up," said Tom Bentz, analyst at ING Futures Derivatives in New York, referring to widely-held views in oil markets that tight heating oil inventories are likely to keep volatility high in oil markets this winter.
November unleaded gained a sharp 2.00 cents a gallon, settling at 65.52 cents a gallon.
That gain did not quite offset unleaded's losses on Thursday of 2.07 cents a gallon, which contributed to trader views downside pressure was likely to be highly featured in next week's trade.
Crude oil for November delivery ended Friday 40 cents higher at $24.66, gaining back just under half of Thursday's losses.

Heating oil, the recent pacesetter of the oil complex, took a bit of a breather Friday, with futures for November delivery settling 0.51 higher at 71.43 cents a gallon, the slighest gain in the oil complex.

Traders said gasoline benefited from industry data earlier in the week showing refinery utilization rates came down last week as did gasoline imports -- two factors that have cursed unleaded recently as the laggard of the complex as heat and and crude have taken off to dizzying heights.

On the heating oil front, market sources were quick to note that any hint of real cold would stoke the market back up to its recent heights and lead crude to bust its 1996 high of $25.70 a barrel set on April 16.
-- Oliver Ludwig, New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1633
